statement.essentials: The facial nerve leaves the skull through a small opening just behind the jaw and ear, and passes straight into the gland.
statement.anatomy: The trunk of the facial nerve invariably emerges from the base of the skull through the stylomastoid foramen and, in most specimens, enters the parotid gland before it divides.
statement.clinical: In 23 formalin-fixed cadavers the nerve emerged through the stylomastoid foramen in every dissection, and divided within the gland in 85% and before entering it in 15%.

limitations: One cadaver series; the point of division varies between people.
